title: Hierarchical Logical Processor on the Rotated Surface Code with Shuttle Buses
authors: Zi-Han Chen, Ming-Cheng Chen, Chao-Yang Lu, Jian-Wei Pan
abstract: Quantum platforms with beyond-planar connectivity provide new opportunities for fault-tolerant quantum computation (FTQC). While quantum low-density parity-check (qLDPC) codes offer high encoding efficiency, their direct implementation requires non-local couplings in every round of syndrome extraction, incurring additional physical error and implementation complexity. To reduce the frequency of such couplings, we propose the Hierarchical Logical Processor (HLP), which concatenates a high-rate quantum CSS code with the rotated surface code (RSC). HLPs can achieve beyond-RSC encoding efficiency while requiring long-range connectivity only once every $Θ(d_0)$ rounds of level-0 error correction, where $d_0$ denotes the base-code distance, substantially reducing the frequency of non-local couplings relative to direct implementations of qLDPC codes. HLPs introduce elongated RSC patches called shuttle buses. Using transversal hybrid-unit CNOT gates, a single shuttle bus can simultaneously couple to multiple standard RSC patches. This capability enables efficient level-1 syndrome extraction with suppressed level-1 error correlations and supports highly parallel logical Pauli measurements. We perform circuit-level simulations of several concrete HLP constructions and benchmark both logical memory and logical Pauli measurement performance. At a physical error rate of $10^{-3}$, an HLP based on the [[256,194,4]] code achieves 3-4 times higher qubit efficiency than the standard RSC. Compared with the yoked surface code on the same level-1 code, this HLP reduces the space overhead per logical qubit by 100-200 physical qubits and shortens the logical error-correction cycle time by a factor of 20-30.
summary: The paper introduces the Hierarchical Logical Processor (HLP) to enhance fault tolerance in quantum computing by combining high-rate codes with the Rotated Surface Code. By using 'shuttle buses' and specific gate scheduling, it drastically reduces the frequency of complex long-range couplings required for error correction. This results in substantial improvements in qubit efficiency and operational speed compared to existing surface code implementations.
main_problem: The primary challenge is achieving fault-tolerant quantum computation (FTQC) with high encoding efficiency while minimizing the frequency and complexity of non-local couplings required for syndrome extraction.
main_result: The proposed Hierarchical Logical Processor (HLP) significantly improves qubit efficiency (3-4 times higher than RSC) and reduces space overhead/cycle time compared to standard surface code implementations.
method: The authors propose concatenating a high-rate quantum CSS code with the Rotated Surface Code, utilizing 'shuttle buses' for parallel syndrome extraction via transversal hybrid-unit CNOT gates.
model_or_system: The model is an HLP architecture built on the Rotated Surface Code (RSC), involving core patches and shuttle buses. It analyzes error suppression through specific compilation parameters ($\alpha_b = d_1, \alpha_c = 1$) during level-1 syndrome extraction.
key_observables: Logical qubit efficiency, space overhead reduction (100-200 physical qubits), logical error rate (LER) decay rates, and cycle time reduction factors (20-30).
important_parameters: Physical error rate ($10^{-3}$), base-code distance ($d_0$), level-1 code distance ($d_1$), and compilation parameters ($\alpha_b, \alpha_c$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on a phenomenological depolarizing noise model and assumes that setting specific compilation parameters effectively suppresses level-1 error correlations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the HLP architecture (cores/shuttle buses), benchmarking memory performance using Iceberg/Square Berg codes, detailing logical Pauli measurement gadgets (H-transformed, HS-transformed), and showing soft-output simulation results for LER extrapolation.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from introducing the HLP concept to proving error suppression via specific gate parameter choices. It then benchmarks memory performance, demonstrates parallel logical measurements using specialized gadgets, and concludes with detailed theoretical bounds on measurement error probabilities.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses resource overheads in large-scale quantum computation by proposing a hierarchical structure that mitigates the need for frequent long-range interactions, which is critical for physical realization on current hardware platforms.
